plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with showy colored bracts that surround small yellow true flowers. In its native range it grows as a tall woody shrub, and it is widely grown as a potted plant elsewhere during the holiday season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide, outdoors in frost-free regions such as California, Florida, Hawaii and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: The colorful parts of a poinsettia are modified leaves called bracts, not petals. Flowering is triggered by long nights, which is why it blooms near the winter solstice.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. Many cultivars open in cool winter weather and brighten gardens when little else is in bloom.
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and China; grown in temperate gardens in the southeastern United States, the UK, Japan and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. It is the official flower of Alabama, where it is called the state flower.

plants.name: Delosperma cooperi
plants.description: A low, mat-forming succulent that is covered in bright daisy-like flowers during the Southern Hemisphere summer. It thrives in full sun and dry, rocky soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to March)
plants.location: Native to South Africa, including the Eastern Cape and Free State highlands
plants.funFact: The flowers open only in bright sunlight and close in the evening or on overcast days. The succulent leaves store water to survive drought.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like leaves and tall stems topped by rounded clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers. It puts on a spectacular display at the height of the Southern Hemisphere summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February)
plants.location: Native to South Africa; widely planted in Australia, New Zealand, Chile and coastal California
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, Agapanthus is not a true lily. Its name comes from the Greek words agape (love) and anthos (flower), and it has become invasive in parts of Australia and New Zealand.
